reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) demonstrates impurity-induced segregation and softening in a TiVNbTa refractory HEA, but the hypothesis extends this mechanism to Ti–Ni–based HEAs without any cited evidence for that specific system. The key premise that the same mechanism operates in Ti–Ni alloys is unsupported, and the cited paper does not address the proposed intervention or its predicted outcome.
premises: Interstitial impurities (O, N) promote nanoscale phase segregation at grain boundaries and in the matrix of HEAs at high temperature
This impurity-induced segregation depletes the matrix of solutes, causing progressive softening
Reducing impurity uptake during processing will suppress such segregation
Suppressing segregation preserves a chemically uniform microstructure that impedes dislocation motion
This will enhance elevated-temperature strength and creep resistance in Ti–Ni–based HEAs
